fix_commit.message: tftp: propagate expired timer from tftp_state_timeout()
fix_commit.author: Joshua Rogers

findings.title: TFTP overall timeout expiry masked by tftp_state_timeout() returning 0 instead of negative value
findings.message: In tftp_state_timeout(), when Curl_timeleft() reports the overall operation time budget has been exhausted (timeout_ms < 0), the function sets state->error = TFTP_ERR_TIMEOUT and state->state = TFTP_STATE_FIN, but then returns the literal value 0 instead of propagating the negative timeout_ms. The sole caller, tftp_multi_statemach(), checks 'if(timeout_ms < 0)' to decide whether to abort the transfer with CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT. Because the return value is forced to 0 (which is not < 0), that abort path is never taken via this check, even though the state was already flagged as FIN/TFTP_ERR_TIMEOUT. This masks the properly detected timeout condition from the caller, defeating the overall-timeout enforcement for TFTP transfers and can allow the state machine to keep the transfer running (spinning in the event loop, potentially indefinitely / until other guards trigger) instead of promptly aborting with a timeout error as intended. This was introduced together with a change of the caller's guard from '<= 0' to '< 0' in the same commit, which made the masking effective (previously any non-positive return, including 0, would trigger the abort).
findings.suggestion: Return the negative timeout_ms value (instead of hard-coded 0) so that the caller's 'if(timeout_ms < 0)' check correctly detects the expired timer and aborts the transfer with CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT as intended.

ground_truth.root_cause: A refactor of the TFTP timeout logic (commit d3d90ad9c0) replaced the old wall-clock deadline comparison with a Curl_timeleft()-based negative-value convention, but in the branch that handles an already-expired timer it kept returning the literal 0 (a holdover from the old code's 'return 0' pattern for absolute timeout) instead of returning the negative timeout_ms. The same commit also tightened the caller's guard from '<= 0' to '< 0', which had previously masked this exact bug (0 used to also trigger the abort). The combination silently disables timeout propagation for the expired-timer branch.
